lead.title: llama.cpp adds Decision Models support with a new /v1/systemone endpoint
lead.summary: llama.cpp merged PR #29818 on October 2, adding a POST /v1/systemone API to llama-server for typed decision models (laya, julia-1, lev, openjev, kev). A model receives a state — text, JSON, or a screenshot for vision-capable weights — plus typed questions and returns a probability for each option in a single forward pass, skipping token-by-token generation. The endpoint follows the Typesafe.ai SystemOne API format and ships with five open GGUF decision models, a relevant new primitive for self-hosted agent and automation stacks.

top_stories.title: Nvidia introduces a 64GB DGX Spark from $4,999 as the 128GB model jumps to $6,950
top_stories.summary: A 64GB GB10 Grace Blackwell tier will be sold from October 23 by Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI, capable of running models up to roughly 100B parameters on-device. It arrives as the memory shortage (the 'RAMpocalypse') pushes the 128GB DGX Spark well above its launch price.

top_stories.title: Micro Center now requires a signed declaration and photo ID to buy an RTX 5090
top_stories.summary: A Micro Center store in Tustin, California began requiring RTX 5090 buyers to sign an anti-scalping/anti-export pledge, show a government ID, and limit purchases to one card per customer, ever — a sign of how tight high-VRAM consumer GPU supply has become under export-control and scalper pressure.

top_stories.title: ThinkingBox grades agents on the database records they leave behind, not their prose
top_stories.summary: Microsoft and Hugging Face released ThinkingBox, an open benchmark that grades AI agents on backend records and side effects rather than generated text, run against isolated MCP tool sessions. It can be self-hosted with its MCP and OpenEnv servers.

top_stories.title: Supabase raises $150M led by GIC and acquires Turso to build AI-agent databases
top_stories.summary: The round includes CapitalG, IronArc and SquarePeg; the Turso acquisition folds a SQLite-based, agent-optimised database into Supabase, which also launched hosted sandboxes for long-running AI agents.

items.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri-1, an open-weight sovereign reasoning MoE
items.summary: An Apache-2.0 mixture-of-experts reasoning model targeting European needs, with strong German and English reasoning, vLLM-ready with FP8 and GGUF quantized variants. Still climbing the Hugging Face trending chart through October 3.

items.title: Cloudflare open-sources Clef and Clef-Flash: multimodal models for typed structured output
items.summary: The 'SystemOne' post-trained family (Clef on Qwen3.8-27B, Clef-Flash on a Qwen3.5 base) does image-text-to-typed-output with schema-constrained structured output and classification, built for agent and guardrail pipelines.

items.title: NaiveAI Naive-N0.5-Flash: MIT-licensed MoE code/long-context model from Beijing
items.summary: The debut open-weights model from Beijing-based NaiveAI — a MoE tuned for code and long-context agentic work, published with weights and inference code, and already spawning quantized GGUF derivatives.

items.title: Jeffy: local pretrained text classifiers that run and retrain on CPU
items.summary: A new GitHub project showcased on Show HN ships pretrained text classifiers that run entirely on CPU, with local retraining on your own labels.

items.title: Valet: self-hosted coding agents in per-thread Docker sandboxes
items.summary: Valet runs Claude Code and Codex coding agents in per-thread sandboxes, deployable with a single docker compose command for fully local agent workflows.

items.title: cliproxy-rs: Rust rewrite of CLIProxyAPI, a local proxy for LLM subscription accounts
items.summary: A drop-in compatible Rust port exposing Claude, Codex, Gemini and OpenAI-compatible providers as a single local proxy endpoint for local clients and agents.

items.title: Home Assistant ships a native llama.cpp conversation integration — guides shift from HACS workarounds to first-party setup
items.summary: Home Assistant 2026.8 added native llama.cpp and LiteLLM conversation integrations, retiring the HACS bridges. Community guides now recommend pointing the integration at any OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint, exposing a minimal set of entities, and letting the built-in intent matcher handle routine commands with the LLM as fallback.

items.title: Piper TTS archived — guides now recommend Kokoro/XTTS and a fully local Whisper + Ollama + Wyoming voice stack
items.summary: An October 2026 guide to the offline voice stack flags that Piper is archived and read-only on GitHub despite running on ~8.9% of Home Assistant installs, recommending Kokoro TTS or Coqui XTTS for new builds — and to verify airgapped operation with a packet capture.

items.title: Open WebUI ecosystem update: oikb knowledge-base sync and the Open WebUI Computer agent harness
items.summary: oikb keeps Knowledge Bases synced with local folders, GitHub repos, S3 and 40+ other sources via incremental SHA-256 diffing, while Open WebUI Computer (cptr) serves your whole machine to any browser and reconnects as a model through its OpenAI-compatible gateway.

items.title: n8n v3 major release (operational cleanup, breaking changes) signalled for ~October 2026
items.summary: n8n's development guide signals a v3 major as an operational release — breaking changes, removals and legacy cleanup. Self-hosters running queue mode with AI nodes should review the v3 changelog before upgrading.

items.title: Local AI mini-PC roundup: DGX Spark vs AMD Strix Halo vs Mac Studio M5, prices re-verified October 3
items.summary: A hands-on comparison of the GB10, Strix Halo and Mac Studio tiers for local LLM inference, with every price re-checked against vendor stores and live listings — evidence that the memory shortage has pushed 128GB unified-memory boxes well above launch prices.

items.title: Analysts say the GPU street-price spike has plateaued; a ~$1,600 RTX 5080 flagged as poor resale value
items.summary: Tech YES City and Moore's Law Is Dead hosts conclude retail GPU pricing has hit a ceiling as buyers resist inflated markups, calling a $1,600 RTX 5080 or an overpriced RTX 5070 Ti an irrational purchase with up to $1,000 of resale value at risk.
